Continuous families expose pdf/logpdf; discrete families expose pmf/logpmf. Every operation has an _array function taking a PHP array as its first argument and the same parameters/defaults, for example:
$probability = Phit\dist_normal_cdf(x: 1.96); // Approximately 0.975.
$tails = Phit\dist_t_sf_array(values: [1, 2, 3], df: 12);
$logMass = Phit\dist_poisson_logpmf_array(counts: [0, 2, 5], lambda: 3.2);
$interval = Phit\dist_gamma_quantile_array(probabilities: [.025, .975], shape: 2, scale: 3);
Scalar continuous evaluation uses argument x; discrete uses k. Batch continuous evaluation uses values; discrete uses counts; all batch quantiles use probabilities. Parameter names are part of the contract because PHP supports named arguments. The generated stubs/phit.php lists every exact signature. Loading the extension makes all functions available globally.
Batch evaluation constructs the distribution once, then streams input values through the same core evaluation policy. Output is a packed list in input iteration order; keys are not retained. Empty input returns [], but parameters are still validated. An invalid element rejects the entire call. No missing rows are dropped. The benchmarks quantify when batching saves PHP boundary overhead and when numerical evaluation dominates.

title: Probability distributions
text:
Tails and likelihoods
Use survival functions for upper tails rather than subtracting a rounded CDF from one. Use log functions directly rather than taking the log of a probability that may already have underflowed.
Phit\dist_normal_sf(10);     // About 7.62e-24; 1 - Phit\dist_normal_cdf(10) is zero.
Phit\dist_normal_logsf(40);  // About -804.61, even though the ordinary SF is zero.
$logLikelihood = array_sum(Phit\dist_poisson_logpmf_array([2, 5, 3, 0], lambda: 2.5));
A density is not a probability at a point and may exceed one. Sum log densities or log masses for independent observations; likelihood underflow is avoided this way. Log probabilities at impossible events are -INF. PHP JSON encoding with JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR rejects nonfinite results; callers must choose their own serialization policy rather than silently replacing numerical values.
The runnable examples/distributions.php demonstrates a two-sided t test, a mean confidence interval, a Poisson likelihood, a central probability, extreme upper tails and equivalent NB parameterizations. The sample data are hypothetical and the computations illustrate the API.

title: Probability distributions
text:
Boundaries and errors
Evaluation points may be ±INF, but NAN raises 1003. Null, numeric strings, booleans and nested array elements are not numeric inputs; malformed batch elements raise 1001. Scalar argument-type failures follow Zend’s runtime conventions. There is no distribution missing option. Nonfinite parameters raise 1003; invalid domains and quantile probabilities outside [0,1] raise 1001. Binomial size above 2^53 raises 1007. A NAN numerical result raises 1006; it is not returned as a value. Parameters so extreme that the incomplete beta or gamma cannot be evaluated also raise 1006 promptly: a beta-type sum \(a + b\) beyond the double range, a beta-type parameter above \(10^{300}\) evaluated within \(10^{-300}\) of an end of the support, or a gamma-type shape or point above \(10^{300}\) (for example dist_f_cdf(2, 3, PHP_FLOAT_MAX) or dist_gamma_cdf(1e30, 1e30)). Earlier builds could hang or panic on such input.
Outside support, density/mass is zero and log density/mass is -INF. Boundary densities can be infinite, for example a beta shape below one at a support endpoint. Discrete PMFs at non-integer counts are zero, while CDF/SF use the floor of the evaluation point. SF always means strictly greater than that count.
Continuous quantile endpoints are the support bounds, including infinities. Discrete quantiles return the smallest support value whose CDF reaches the requested probability, using a documented 64 * EPSILON relative comparison allowance on the smaller tail to accommodate rounding at CDF steps. Endpoint p=0 follows the conventional lower support bound; p=1 follows the upper support bound for ordinary distributions. A point mass returns its actual mass location at p=1. This differs from R/SciPy in some degenerate cases. Returned count quantiles are PHP floats; precision is limited by binary64’s exact integer range.

title: Probability distributions
text:
Numerical implementation and dependency audit
The raw statrs audit evaluates the saved R cases with statrs 0.19, using log(CDF)/log(SF) because that crate has no log-tail API. In these cases it loses small tails, has roughly 4.8e-4 relative binomial CDF error at size one million, and suffers inaccurate extreme quantiles. Those findings motivated a separate distribution module while retaining existing estimator numerical paths.








Families
Probability backend

Normal, lognormal

Student t, F, beta

Stable densities; log-scale gamma series/fraction

expm1, log1p and stable softplus formulas



The runtime pins MIT-licensed cdflib = 0.4.3; GPL nmath ports were excluded by the dependency audit. statrs remains the estimator dependency and a source of special functions/seeds where appropriate. The implementation forms both tails independently and uses custom log-scale expansions below 1e-280. Continuous quantiles use log-tail Newton steps protected by brackets. No R/Python/BLAS runtime dependency is introduced. Numerical failure is explicit; this is not proof of accuracy for every finite argument or arbitrarily extreme shape parameter.

title: Probability distributions
text:
Reference evidence and release scope
The executed comparison records R, SciPy and 60-digit mpmath references, documented boundary differences and quantity-specific tolerances. Scalar/batch identities and validation run in the offline release gate. Performance evidence covers 1,000, 100,000 and one million values, including peak process memory and regression preservation.
Random sampling uses explicitly seeded dist_{family}_rng(n, seed, ...parameters) calls with local ChaCha20 state. The sampling contract documents reproducibility, validation and independent reference vectors. The readiness assessment records this implementation, the estimator reuse experiment and remaining publication/platform gates.

title: Design philosophy
text:
The native interface should be as vanilla as possible: ordinary PHP arrays of numbers in, an associative array of numbers and numeric arrays out. A caller should be able to understand a fit from the function signature, the data shapes, and the documented statistical conventions. Loading the extension makes the functions available without application-specific imports or model classes.
For all estimators, the raw interface is a supplied design matrix x and outcome vector y. Each row is an observation and each column is a predictor. The PHP binding adds a fixed intercept by default; intercept: false accepts a complete literal design. The Rust core and random-effect designs remain literal matrices. This small, explicit convenience keeps the usual application call simple. The extension checks those inputs and performs the estimation; it does not infer how the application’s source data should be interpreted. Invalid values produce errors. Missing null/NAN values use documented listwise deletion with a warning and sample metadata; callers can choose strict rejection.
Use explicit numerical defaults and document them. Current inference is homoskedastic OLS with 95% t intervals, and logistic, probit and Poisson maximum likelihood with 95% normal Wald intervals; rank deficiency is rejected. Undefined statistics remain NAN/INF in the raw output. Missing-data handling is explicit in the contract and observable in every fit result. Keep the mathematical calculations visible and understandable in the Rust core.

title: Design philosophy
text:
The native interface should be as vanilla as possible: ordinary PHP arrays of numbers in, an associative array of numbers and numeric arrays out. A caller should be able to understand a fit from the function signature, the data shapes, and the documented statistical conventions. Loading the extension makes the functions available without application-specific imports or model classes.
For all estimators, the raw interface is a supplied design matrix x and outcome vector y. Each row is an observation and each column is a predictor. The PHP binding adds a fixed intercept by default; intercept: false accepts a complete literal design. The Rust core and random-effect designs remain literal matrices. This small, explicit convenience keeps the usual application call simple. The extension checks those inputs and performs the estimation; it does not infer how the application’s source data should be interpreted. Invalid values produce errors. Missing null/NAN values use documented listwise deletion with a warning and sample metadata; callers can choose strict rejection.
Use explicit numerical defaults and document them. Current inference is homoskedastic OLS with 95% t intervals, and logistic, probit and Poisson maximum likelihood with 95% normal Wald intervals; rank deficiency is rejected. Undefined statistics remain NAN/INF in the raw output. Missing-data handling is explicit in the contract and observable in every fit result. Keep the mathematical calculations visible and understandable in the Rust core.

title: Design philosophy
section: Convenience belongs around the raw call

title: Design philosophy
text:
Implementation boundaries
Use established Rust-native numerical crates by default. Keep the implementation and build straightforward until a concrete requirement calls for an external BLAS/LAPACK dependency. A backend change should address a demonstrated numerical, performance or deployment need and preserve the input/output contract and reference agreement. We tried Apple Accelerate without a speed advantage on our current workloads, then removed the experimental path. The benchmark evidence remains documented.
stats-core owns estimation, inference and numerical validation. It accepts Rust vectors and returns an a dedicated result struct or StatsError without PHP types. Established crates supply matrix decompositions and distributions; our code expresses the statistical formulas.
php-extension owns PHP value inspection, numeric conversion, registration, exception conversion, missing-row filtering with warnings/accounting, and output construction. Keep it thin; missing-data handling does not change the estimator. Data ingestion and application presentation remain outside the statistical engine.
Prefer the simplest correct solution, small focused functions, documented contracts and reference evidence. Numerical correctness, working software and educational clarity take priority over architecture or speculative extensibility.

title: Design philosophy
text:
Current scope and change decisions
The current scope is OLS, binomial logistic/probit regression, Poisson count regression, and Gaussian mixed ML/REML with explicit random-design terms, and binomial random-intercept marginal ML. The user has expanded the goal toward R/lme4 compatibility; the coverage ledger records implemented and remaining functionality. Each fitter is a dedicated implementation, without a general GLM framework. Keep data preparation and presentation around the plain numerical API. Expand numerical functionality through explicit contracts and reference evidence. Additional optimization algorithms now address actual multivariate variance estimation; they do not justify a general statistical framework. Avoid speculative layers, backend interfaces or a large PHP object API. Do not introduce generic Model, Family, Link or Optimizer traits for hypothetical future work.
For a proposed feature, first ask whether it changes estimation or merely makes application data easier to prepare. Preparation belongs in an optional layer. A numerical feature needs a concrete use case, an explicit contract and suitable verification before it expands the engine. Extra dependencies and abstractions must solve a demonstrated problem.
Keep contracts.qmd aligned with implementation and verification.qmd aligned with actual test evidence. Each implemented estimator should have a math walkthrough notebook and a verification document showing equivalent fits in R, statsmodels and this extension where supported. This philosophy governs future work; it does not imply that helpers or additional models already exist.
The posterior-draw operations are explicit numerical kernels for a separate CmdStan interface’s moment matching: weighted moments, covariance maps and affine transforms. Literal row/parameter order and strict validation apply to all three; they never insert an intercept or drop missing rows. Stan evaluation, PSIS, iteration control and diagnostics remain the consuming package’s responsibility. See the numerical contract and reference evidence.

title: Design philosophy
section: Learning examples use meaningful simulated data
text:
Learning examples use meaningful simulated data
Use reproducible simulations with named variables, units, plausible ranges, noise, and intentional relationships for the main learning examples. Label them as synthetic, state the generating equation and seed, and save the observations so Rust, PHP, R and statsmodels fit exactly the same sample. Report observed sample correlations rather than treating the intended relationship as an empirical result. Explain that correlation does not establish causation.
Distinguish observed inputs, constructed columns (such as intercept ones), true generating parameters, trial coefficients, and estimated coefficients. Display matrix dimensions and intermediate values beside the mathematical steps. Use small samples for readable matrix displays and explain their statistical limits. Keep simple sequences and hand-checkable arrays for focused numerical tests where they help expose an edge case; they should not be the main story in a walkthrough.
The current shared teaching sample is simulated housing in docs/data/housing.csv, generated by tests/generate-learning-data.R. Its correlations are intentional, and both one-predictor and correlated two-predictor fits have R reference fixtures.

title: Design philosophy
text:
Performance evidence
Maintain a reproducible API-level benchmark against R and Python statsmodels for each implemented estimator where reference support exists. Verify numerical agreement on identical simulated inputs before publishing timings. Use release builds, materialize inference and observation-level outputs, and record versions, machine details, thread settings, raw measurements and timing boundaries. Separate fitting from loading and runtime startup; record process memory where available. Benchmarks are explicit development commands rather than unit tests. See the OLS report and logistic report. Measurements inform decisions; they do not justify speculative optimizations or additional runtime dependencies.
The logistic teaching sample is saved in docs/data/learning.csv, generated by tests/generate-logistic-fixtures.R. It uses correlated study hours and practice scores, with Bernoulli pass/fail draws from explicitly stated generating probabilities.
Mixed models begin with one Gaussian random intercept, a continuous outcome and explicit group labels. Keep marginal likelihood, variance components and conditional group estimates visible in code. REML, random slopes and multiple grouping factors now have separate contracts, R optimizer fixtures and an executed math walkthrough. Native BOBYQA and Nelder–Mead use established pinned Rust crates; exact NLopt/PORT backend support remains open.
For non-Gaussian mixed models, distinguish implementation agreement from integration accuracy. Document the likelihood approximation, compare like methods against R, and assess node-count sensitivity with an independent integrator. The binomial random-intercept milestone makes this explicit before expanding Poisson likelihoods or general random-term designs.

title: Deploying to servers
text: The deployed PHP process needs only phit.so and its system libraries. Rust, Clang, PIE, R and Python are build or development tools and are not needed at runtime. Installation covers PIE and the prebuilt binaries; this page covers PHP-FPM, containers and manual builds.

title: Deploying to servers
text:
Names

Composer and PIE package: phpstats/phit.
Registered extension: phit. Use it with extension_loaded('phit'), phpversion('phit'), get_extension_funcs('phit') and Composer’s ext-phit.
Installed module: phit.so. A direct Cargo build produces libphit.so on Linux and libphit.dylib on macOS; they are the same extension.
Functions are in the Phit namespace, such as Phit\fit_lm.

title: Deploying to servers
text:
Supported targets
The extension supports PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5, non-thread-safe, on Linux and macOS. Windows and ZTS builds are not supported. The prebuilt binaries target Debian Bookworm with glibc on x86_64 and aarch64. Alpine (musl) and older glibc releases need a PIE or manual build. CI tests Linux x86_64 and aarch64 at all three PHP versions, and macOS on Apple silicon.

title: Deploying to servers
text:
PHP-FPM
PHP loads the extension when a process starts. After installing or replacing phit.so:

Enable it in the configuration PHP-FPM reads. php --ini shows the CLI’s files, which can differ from FPM’s.
Restart the PHP-FPM service so every worker loads the new module.
Check the web runtime, not only the CLI, for example with extension_loaded('phit') and phpversion('phit') in a request.

Each call converts PHP arrays into Rust vectors, fits the model and returns an array within the request. No background process, subprocess or network service is involved.

title: Deploying to servers
text:
A PHP-FPM container image
docker/Dockerfile builds a PHP-FPM image with the extension installed. From the repository root:
docker build --target checks -f docker/Dockerfile -t phit:checks .
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t phit:local .
./scripts/check-container phit:local phit:checks
The build installs the extension through PIE 1.5.0 and runs the Rust and PHP checks. The isolated FPM check sends a real FastCGI request. The production-image check then exercises both CLI and FPM using the shipped PHP configuration and verifies identical OLS coefficients and a Poisson log-exposure fit.
The final image contains the PHP runtime and installed extension. Rust, Clang, PIE, Python, repository sources, and test utilities remain in the build stages. The image retains the official PHP entrypoint and foreground PHP-FPM command. Use it as an application base:
FROM phit:local
COPY app/ /var/www/html/
Connect your normal web server to FPM. FPM speaks FastCGI, not HTTP; no public FPM listener is needed for the tests. The verification script removes only its own temporary container and never edits a production PHP/FPM configuration.

Build pins and reproducibility
The Dockerfile pins PHP and Rust base images by OCI digest. The workflow records separate PHP 8.3/8.4/8.5 image digests. Build and runtime stages share exactly the same PHP image. Cargo.lock pins Rust dependencies; the downloaded PIE PHAR has a pinned SHA-256. Update those pins deliberately and rerun the gate.
Debian APT packages are resolved at build time. These pins establish a repeatable base and dependency selection, not a promise that every future rebuild has the same bytes. Binary manifests record the compiler, PHP API, architecture, libc, linked libraries, extension hash and Cargo.lock hash.

title: Deploying to servers
text:
Manual build without PIE
From a checkout of the repository or the release’s source archive, the standard phpize build works without PIE. pie/config.m4 and pie/Makefile.frag run the locked Cargo build:
cd pie
/path/to/phpize
./configure --with-php-config=/path/to/php-config
make -j4
# Stage without modifying the installed PHP runtime:
make install INSTALL_ROOT=/absolute/path/to/staging
# Or install after reviewing the build:
# sudo make install
Build as an unprivileged user before installing. The install goal requires the already built module and does not rerun Cargo under sudo. INSTALL_ROOT stages under the configured extension directory. On macOS, use the matching LLVM/header setup in the development guide.
Add extension=phit.so to the relevant PHP INI configuration after a manual install. Inspect php --ini for CLI; check the FPM configuration separately. Verify the native functions through both. Rebuild for another PHP ABI, architecture, thread-safety/debug configuration, or platform.

title: API overview
text:
The extension registers the PHP module phit (extension=phit, Composer ext-phit). Every function is in the Phit namespace and is named by prefix.
Import the functions you use:
stubs/phit.php in the repository declares every signature with PHPDoc array shapes for IDEs and static analysis. Do not load it at runtime.

title: API overview
API overview
text:
Formula interfaces
The formula functions parse an R model formula, build R’s model.matrix() over named columns, and call the estimation cores of fit_ols, fit_logistic, fit_probit, fit_poisson, fit_mixed, and fit_logistic_mixed. Each fit returns the complete result contract of its matrix function. It adds formula, response, columns (coefficient names in coefficient order), terms, assign, intercept, and named (column => coefficient). fit_glm and fit_glmer also return family and link. model_matrix returns y, x (including the (Intercept) column), the naming keys, offset, random designs in the shape fit_mixed accepts, and the deletion accounting.
Missing-value deletion covers only the variables a formula uses, with the same warning, missing: 'raise' behavior, and row accounting as the matrix functions. model_matrix keeps unused factor levels, as model.matrix() does. The fitting functions drop them, as lm(), glm(), and lme4 do. Unknown columns, malformed factor descriptors, referenced list-columns, and invalid formulas raise 1001. Column-length mismatch raises 1002. Infinite transform results raise 1003. Unsupported functions, families, links, and random-effect structures raise 1007. Rank deficiency raises 1004. The formula guide defines the syntax, contrasts, data shapes, verification, and every known difference from R.

title: API overview
text:
Matrix model contracts
Matrix model functions defines the inputs, results, convergence rules and failure cases of each matrix function:

OLS
Binary logistic regression
Probit regression
Poisson regression
Gaussian random-intercept mixed model
Weights, offsets and grouped binomial responses
General Gaussian mixed model
Binomial random-intercept model

title: API overview
text:
Fixed intercept
The seven matrix estimators take bool $intercept = true. Supply predictor columns only: the binding prepends an exact ones column and the estimated intercept is coefficient 0, followed by predictors in supplied column order. Covariance, standard errors, tests and intervals follow that same order. Parameter counts and residual degrees of freedom include the added coefficient. No input array is mutated.
intercept: false passes the supplied x matrix literally. It is both the opt-out for a through-origin model and the compatibility option for callers already supplying a complete design with ones. There is no automatic detection of existing constant columns: leaving ones in x with the default creates a duplicate intercept and a rank-deficiency error, rather than silently guessing intent.
For an intercept-only fit, supply one empty predictor row per outcome, such as x: array_fill(0, count($y), []). An empty sample or ragged matrix is still invalid; empty predictor rows require intercept: true. Missing-row validation and deletion still apply to outcomes, predictors, groups, weights and offsets before fitting.
The Rust core takes the design literally.
Random-effect designs random[*].z remain explicit; this option only constructs the fixed design. For a random intercept/slope, z still needs [1, slope] rows.

title: API overview
text:
Errors and conversion
The binding accepts actual integers and floats as numeric elements, with null and NAN representing missingness. PHP integers are converted to f64, so integers beyond the exact range of double precision may lose precision. Array keys and names do not label coefficients: row order aligns x with y, and column order aligns all coefficient results. Callers should normally supply packed lists and keep labels separately.
Missing values use listwise deletion by default, with one E_WARNING on a successful fit that omits rows. missing: ‘raise’ rejects missingness. Values are not coerced from strings, columns are not added, and aliased predictors are not removed. fitted and residuals follow retained_rows order. See missing-data.qmd for validation order, warnings, accounting and application handling. Applications can promote PHP warnings to exceptions.
Statistical and input failures use PHP Exception with stable numeric codes 1001–1008; see the diagnostic/error contract. There are no estimator-specific exception classes. Callers can inspect getCode() and should handle Throwable at their application boundary, since PHP argument and runtime errors use their own types. Message text may change. If the extension is absent, the functions themselves are unavailable; that is an installation failure rather than an invalid-data result.
NAN/INF are floating-point values in successful results, not failure sentinels. Serialization helpers may map them to null using a documented policy, while the native result preserves them. Current arithmetic uses f64; it is not arbitrary precision, and extreme input scales can exceed its range.

title: API overview
text:
Rust boundary
pub fn fit_ols(
    x: Vec<Vec<f64>>,
    y: Vec<f64>,
) -> Result<OlsResult, StatsError>
The core owns its inputs and has no PHP dependency. OlsResult exposes the same statistical fields as the PHP array (sample-deletion metadata is PHP-only), with Vec for numeric lists, Vec<Vec> for covariance, Vec<[f64; 2]> for confidence intervals, f64 for scalars, and usize for residual degrees of freedom. StatsError implements Display and Error. The binding converts errors and values without implementing statistical formulas.
See design-philosophy.qmd for the boundary between this raw API and optional convenience layers.

title: API overview
text:
Diagnostics and error codes
Every successful estimator returns diagnostics:







Diagnostic key
Contract




converged
true on successful return, including direct OLS; failed fitting throws


solver
scaled_svd, newton_irls, fisher_scoring, profile_variance_search, bobyqa or nelder_mead


iterations, evaluations
Present only when the corresponding historical top-level key exists; same value, not a second counter


gradient_max
Present for logistic mixed only; same scaled-coordinate finite-difference score as its top-level key


boundary, singular
Present when the estimator already reports that flag; legitimate zero variance is permitted


warnings
list; missing-row deletion, a reported near-singular covariance, or the logistic-mixed Laplace approximation advisory



Warnings in this array are interpretation notices. Only listwise deletion also emits the existing single PHP E_WARNING. Missing/undefined diagnostics are omitted; there is no fabricated iteration count or universal score. General Gaussian convergence still uses optimizer termination, parameter bounds, valid factors and finite output; it does not have a final variance-parameter gradient/Hessian gate. OLS has no iterative optimizer. Normal/Wald inference and local convergence do not guarantee model adequacy or quadrature accuracy.
Statistical and input failures throw PHP Exception with a numeric getCode():








Code
Rust ErrorKind
Meaning




1001
InvalidInput
Type/domain/control error, missing=‘raise’, invalid groups/weights/counts


1002
DimensionMismatch
Shape/alignment or insufficient residual observations


1003
Nonfinite
Nonfinite values or arithmetic beyond floating-point range, including nonzero residual variance underflow


1004
RankDeficiency
Numerical design/information rank failure


1005
FactorizationFailure
Required linear solve or positive-definite information factor fails


1006
Nonconvergence
Budget/line-search/optimizer/score failure, separation or unsupported finite optimum at a search boundary


1007
Unsupported
Explicit size/count limit or unimplemented configuration


1008
Internal
Required decomposition output missing or an internal mathematical invariant fails



Messages remain explanatory, not stable machine identifiers. Validation can report the first failed check when multiple problems exist; combined validation checks may use the most relevant category. Zend argument TypeError, result conversion/runtime errors, and caught Rust panics are runtime errors rather than statistical codes. Invalid data are checked before listwise deletion. Rust StatsError::new(kind, message) carries the explicit enum without classifying message text; .0 remains the display message and kind() exposes its category.
Binomial calls limit trials to 1,000,000 per original row, and accepted success-count rounding is canonicalized with round(y*trials)/trials. For exact zero-variance OLS, the existing NaN/INF conventions remain; nonzero variance underflow instead throws 1003. JSON consumers must handle documented undefined OLS quantities explicitly; PHP’s JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR rejects NaN/INF. See the v0.1 assessment for compatibility notes and tested stress ranges.

title: Probit regression scale validation and performance
text:
What is timed?
Workers load the same CSV once, perform one untimed warm-up, and measure five full fits. Each timed fit materializes coefficients, covariance, standard errors, normal z tests, p-values, Wald intervals, every fitted probability and response residual, likelihood, deviance, null deviance, AIC and residual degrees of freedom. PHP also converts inputs and all outputs and constructs row metadata within the timer. Startup, CSV loading, data generation and final JSON serialization are excluded.
R uses formula/model construction and QR-based IRLS, with epsilon 1e-16 to stabilize covariance agreement. Python uses GLM IRLS with parameter tolerance 1e-11; PHP uses weighted SVD Fisher-scoring updates and its documented convergence rules. Starting values, linear solves and stopping criteria differ. This is a comparison of complete public API calls, not equal iteration counts or isolated decomposition speeds. Common numerical-library thread variables are set to one; installed backends and requested settings are recorded. Workers run separately with order alternated between cases. Other machine activity can affect measurements. R’s elapsed timer has coarse millisecond resolution for small cases.

title: Probit regression scale validation and performance
text:
Simulation and agreement
NumPy RNG seed 20261011 generates study hours uniformly between 1 and 12, practice scores as clipped 45 + 3 × hours + normal noise with standard deviation 8, and independent standard-normal extra scores. Binary outcomes are draws from
\[\pi_i=\Phi(-1.9+0.13\,\mathrm{hours}_i+0.011\,\mathrm{score}_i
+0.08\sum_j\mathrm{extra}_{ij}),\qquad y_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_i).\]
This simulation is separate from the small R-generated teaching sample; its scores are unrounded and its seed is different. Every runtime reads identical 17-significant-digit CSV values. Data hashes, generating coefficients and sample correlations are recorded. All coefficient-level quantities and scalar statistics are compared with R at tolerance 1e-9 + 1e-7 × abs(reference). Full fitted/residual vectors are materialized; cross-runtime comparison samples ten evenly spaced rows, while small fixtures check complete vectors. PHP convergence must be true and its update count must be between one and 100. Wald intervals use R confint.default(), and the null baseline follows the documented intercept convention. Probit covariance uses expected Fisher information in all three runtimes.

title: OLS scale validation and performance
text: We compare the public PHP extension, R lm(), and Python statsmodels OLS on identical simulated observations. The extension uses a release build. The results JSON records every timing sample, versions, input hashes, numerical outputs, agreement errors and machine information.

title: OLS scale validation and performance
text:
Recorded results

from pathlib import Path
import json
import pandas as pd

# Keep display order independent of the benchmark worker execution order.
def ordered_table(rows):
    table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    table["implementation"] = pd.Categorical(
        table["implementation"], categories=["R", "statsmodels", "PHP"], ordered=True)
    return table.sort_values(["observations", "coefficients", "implementation"]).reset_index(drop=True)

ROOT = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "Cargo.toml").exists())
report = json.loads((ROOT / "docs/benchmarks/ols-results.json").read_text())
print("Recorded:", report["recorded_at"])
print("Machine:", report["cpu"], "—", report["platform"])
print("Rust:", report["rust"])

Simulation and numerical agreement
NumPy’s default RNG uses seed 20261011 for each case. Area is uniform between 35 and 110 square metres; bedrooms depend on area plus noise, rounded and bounded to 1–4. Wider models add independent standard-normal amenity scores. Fictional monthly rent follows
\[y_i=650+18\,\mathrm{area}_i+60\,\mathrm{bedrooms}_i
+0.5\sum_j\mathrm{amenity}_{ij}+\epsilon_i,
\qquad\epsilon_i\sim N(0,180^2).\]
These are synthetic observations. This generating model includes a bedroom effect; the small teaching notebook deliberately has an area-only generating equation. Large samples contain fresh observations rather than copies of the eight teaching rows. Residual df is checked exactly. Full fitted/residual vectors are calculated, but cross-runtime verification samples ten evenly spaced observations rather than exporting every value. Small reference tests compare full vectors. Extremely small p-values can underflow; the absolute tolerance does not establish relative tail accuracy.

Reproduce and maintain

Future estimators should maintain equivalent R/statsmodels comparisons where supported: shared simulated inputs, complete requested outputs, numerical checks, release builds, raw timings, versions, machine details and stated boundaries. Run this suite when changing numerical implementation. Keep observed results with verification evidence; optimize only when measurements establish a need.

title: OLS scale validation and performance
text:
Apple Accelerate experiment
Historical experiment: the optional macOS accelerate feature was removed after choosing to keep the numerical engine Rust-native until a concrete need justifies an external backend. This section preserves the observed results, not a currently available build option.
The trial replaced the column-scaled SVD with Apple Accelerate’s LAPACK DGESDD in thin mode. PHP conversion, validation, rank threshold, coefficient solving, covariance and inference remain shared. This experiment accelerates the decomposition; it does not route every nalgebra matrix multiplication through BLAS. The default build stays portable Rust.
Both variants passed the Rust R-reference and invalid-input tests. The Accelerate extension also passed PHP integration tests. The following independently timed runs use identical generated CSVs, verified by their hashes; both check numerical agreement with R and statsmodels using the same tolerances and sampled outputs. The Accelerate raw results accompany the archived baseline, with separate extension hashes and every timing sample.

A ratio above 1 means the Accelerate variant was faster in this run. These are two sequential five-repeat experiments, not randomized paired trials. Variation in the R/Python control measurements helps show why small differences should not be treated as conclusive. Matrix shape matters, and PHP input/output allocation still contributes to complete-fit time and memory.
Observed outcome: this experiment did not establish a speed advantage for Accelerate on these shapes. The 100,000-row, three-coefficient case was roughly tied; the million-row case took about 133 ms with Accelerate versus 113 ms with nalgebra, and the eleven-coefficient case took about 42 ms versus 40 ms. The nalgebra implementation is now the sole maintained path. The experimental feature and LAPACK dependencies were removed; recorded results remain available. These timings alone do not isolate decomposition time from PHP conversion or native allocations, so they do not establish the cause of the differences.
Symbol inspection reveals a backend-interface difference: the Rust lapack bindings call _dgesdd_, while this NumPy installation calls _dgesdd$NEWLAPACK$ILP64. Both link Apple’s Accelerate framework, but these are different LAPACK interfaces. This trial therefore does not establish how Rust would perform through NumPy’s newer interface, nor whether that difference caused the observed timings. The report records the imported symbols; only the legacy LAPACK binding was used for this trial.
The historical reports retain individual timings, input hashes, imported symbols and artifact hashes. Their implementation is no longer maintained in this checkout; there is no current accelerate build feature. Keeping a separate archived baseline preserves this comparison when the standard Rust/R/statsmodels report is refreshed. Linux/OpenBLAS was not implemented or verified by this experiment.

title: Binomial random-intercept scale checks and performance
text:
This benchmark fits the same Laplace marginal ML model in R lme4, an independent Python/SciPy reference implementation, and the native PHP extension. It uses shared deterministic binary data, correlated study/practice predictors, three fixed coefficients and 50 groups at 1,000, 10,000 and 100,000 observations.
The Python worker is our likelihood/optimizer reference, not statsmodels’ Bayesian mixed-model estimator and not an optimized Python GLMM package. These measurements compare the named implementations; they do not establish a general Rust-versus-Python speed ranking.

title: Binomial random-intercept scale checks and performance
text:
Timing boundaries and correctness
Each worker loads the same CSV, performs one warm-up fit, then runs three timed fits. PHP times the complete native call, including conversion and all returned inference/observation arrays. R/Python materialize covariance, standard errors, conditional modes and full fixed/conditional fitted values and residuals. Compact sample output and JSON serialization happen outside the timed fit. Process time includes startup, CSV load, warm-up and all timed fits; peak RSS covers the whole worker process. Threads are pinned to one.
Every report is published only after coefficients, covariance/standard errors, group SD/modes, normalized likelihood and common observation samples agree. Likelihood tolerance is absolute 1e-6 plus relative 1e-8; inference uses absolute 2e-5 plus relative 2e-3; estimates use absolute 2e-5 plus relative 2e-4. Group modes use absolute 5e-5 because large-sample flat-profile optimization produced shifts around 2e-5 in modes near zero; relative error there is not informative.
The installed lme4 version disables derivative checks automatically at large n. The benchmark explicitly enables the final joint Hessian. Its initial BOBYQA run also stopped short on the 10,000-row case; an R-only restart from that fit, with rhobeg=0.001 and nAGQ0initStep=FALSE, resolved it. Both R stages are included in its fit time. The report records these controls, versions and data/binary hashes. Native estimates never seed the R worker.

title: Posterior-draw scale validation and performance
text:
Reproduction and timing boundaries
Build using the matching PHP/header environment, then run:
cargo build -p phit --release --locked
# R and jsonlite are benchmark-only development dependencies.
PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php python3 tests/benchmarks/run-draws.py
# Optional overrides: RSCRIPT, STATS_EXTENSION; --repeats 5 --output /path/report.json
Python 3’s standard library generates inputs with random.Random(20261012). Draws have a shared Gaussian component, independent Gaussian noise and parameter means increasing by 0.1. Nonuniform weights have deterministic zeros every 11th row. Covariances are constructed from deterministic full-rank lower factors. The affine matrix includes off-diagonal mixing and a reflection, with a nonzero shift. Temporary JSON inputs are identical for PHP and R; their SHA-256 hashes are retained in the report. No intercept column is added.
Each worker loads JSON once. Startup, input generation, JSON parsing/serialization and reference comparison are outside timed calls. Input loading is recorded separately. Both APIs compute complete result arrays/matrices in each timed call; PHP includes native input conversion, validation and result allocation. Timings also include ordinary runtime reclamation of prior results.
R’s elapsed timer has millisecond resolution. Each map measurement batches 1,000 calls. Moments/affine batch 1,000 calls for the 1,000 × 4 case, 100 for 4,000 × 16, and 10 for both larger cases; the reported value divides by the batch count. This avoids zero small-call readings but still limits R timing precision. R’s garbage collection and machine load contribute variation; raw measurements are available for review. This run does not measure peak memory, Linux, PHP-FPM, Stan evaluation, PSIS or complete moment-matching iterations.

title: Distribution performance and regression preservation
text: The distribution benchmark compares a PHP scalar loop, one native PHP batch call, an internal Rust loop, vectorized R and SciPy on identical saved temporary inputs. It covers 1,000, 100,000 and one million values for normal CDF/SF, Student-t quantile, binomial/Poisson log-PMF, mean/variance, beta quantile and chi-square CDF with df one million. Raw results retain every measurement, numerical summary, input hash, runtime version, thread setting and peak resident memory.

title: Distribution performance and regression preservation
text:
Numerical comparisons before timings
All input cases are verified across implementations before any timing phase begins. Seventeen evenly spaced output values plus min/max use the distribution fixture tolerance: 1e-300 + 1e-12*abs(reference), or 1e-15 + 1e-12*abs(reference) for quantiles. Sum and sum-of-squares consume all outputs, with tolerance 1e-9 + 1e-10*abs(reference) to allow different accumulation orders. Mean/variance outputs are checked directly. R is the benchmark reference; the separate R/SciPy/mpmath record adjudicates reference differences and tests extreme/boundary values more broadly.

title: Distribution performance and regression preservation
text:
Timing boundaries and interpretation
Each worker loads/parses inputs once, performs one untimed warm-up, and measures five repetitions. Distribution calls allocate and populate the complete output vector. The PHP scalar loop constructs a distribution and crosses the PHP/native boundary for each value; batch calls construct it once and stream values natively. The internal Rust loop uses the same validation and an allocated result vector. Descriptive mean/variance has one PHP native call; there is no invented scalar-loop equivalent for those operations.
JSON I/O, startup and output summaries are outside timed calls. PHP input/output conversion and native validation are included. R/SciPy start with native numeric vectors. Runtime reclamation/garbage collection of prior results contributes to the observed API cost. Peak RSS is the whole worker process, including imports, JSON parsing, inputs, outputs and summaries, not isolated kernel memory. Process elapsed time and input loading time are recorded separately.
R’s timer has millisecond resolution. Small distribution cases batch 100 calls; mean/variance batch enough calls to process at least ten million input values per measurement, with a minimum of ten calls. Per-call times divide by the batch count. All raw timings must be positive. Thread environment variables are fixed to one for OpenBLAS, OpenMP, MKL, Accelerate and BLIS; they do not make different numerical implementations identical. PHP scalar/batch worker order alternates by case. Machine load, timer precision and GC make these measurements evidence for these workloads rather than universal speed claims.

Native Rust optimization
The first implementation repeatedly whitened and SVD-factorized all n rows at every trial variance ratio. The optimized implementation follows lme4’s penalized least-squares elimination idea: separate within-group deviations from group means and cache an augmented QR square-root summary. Each trial now factors p+1+G rows. Covariance is computed only for the selected solution. title: Random-intercept Gaussian ML scale validation and performance
text:
Simulation and numerical checks
NumPy RNG seed 20261011 generates correlated study hours and prior scores, independent standard-normal extra predictors, and schools with roughly equal sizes. Outcomes follow
\[y_i=50+1.8\,\mathrm{hours}_i+0.2\,\mathrm{prior}_i
+0.5\sum_j\mathrm{extra}_{ij}+b_{g(i)}+\epsilon_i,
\quad b_g\sim N(0,6^2),\quad\epsilon_i\sim N(0,5^2).\]
This sample is separate from the saved small teaching dataset. Identical 17-significant-digit CSVs are used by every worker. All coefficient-level fields, variance components, ICC, likelihood/AIC and all group effects are checked. Observation-length outputs are fully materialized, but cross-runtime checks sample ten evenly spaced rows; small fixtures check every row.
Benchmark absolute tolerance is 1e-7. Relative tolerance is 1e-6 for ordinary outputs, 1e-5 for covariance, SE, z-statistics, variance components, sigma and ICC, and 1e-9 for likelihood/AIC. Small saved references use the tighter uniform 1e-7 + 1e-6 × abs(reference) policy.
The first 100,000-row check found R’s between-group variance differed from the analytic-score solution by about 2.6e-6 relative while log-likelihood differed by only about 8e-10. The log-ratio profile score was approximately 2.55e-4 in R, -1.88e-6 in Python and 3.12e-11 in Rust. A flat likelihood and floating-point objective resolution limit independently optimized variance-component agreement; the variance-sensitive benchmark tolerances reflect that measured distinction. They do not replace the closed-form ML check or justify relaxing likelihood agreement. The finite Rust profile grid itself is not a global-optimum proof.

title: Poisson regression scale validation and performance
text:
What is timed?
Workers load the same CSV once, perform one untimed warm-up, and measure five full fits. Each timed fit materializes coefficients, covariance, standard errors, normal z tests, p-values, Wald intervals, every fitted mean count and response residual, likelihood, deviance, null deviance, AIC and residual degrees of freedom. PHP also converts inputs and all outputs and constructs row metadata within the timer. Startup, CSV loading, data generation and final JSON serialization are excluded.
R uses formula/model construction and QR-based IRLS, with epsilon 1e-16 to stabilize covariance agreement. Python uses GLM IRLS with parameter tolerance 1e-11; PHP uses weighted SVD Newton updates and its documented convergence rules. Starting values, linear solves and stopping criteria differ. This is a comparison of complete public API calls, not equal iteration counts or isolated decomposition speeds. Common numerical-library thread variables are set to one; installed backends and requested settings are recorded. Workers run separately with order alternated between cases. Other machine activity can affect measurements. R’s elapsed timer has coarse millisecond resolution for small cases.

title: Seeded sampling verification and performance
text: The sampling API uses local ChaCha20 state and inverse CDFs. This benchmark times full PHP batches for normal, beta and Poisson at 1,000, 100,000 and one million draws. Every call reinitializes the explicit seed and allocates the complete numeric output. Raw results retain the seed, input hashes, numerical evidence, PHP version, binary hash, all timing samples, process elapsed time and peak RSS.

title: Seeded sampling verification and performance
text:
Independent verification first
Before any timing phase, Python independently computes the ChaCha blocks at 17 evenly spaced indices, with the pinned PCG seed expansion/Open01 mapping. Base-R quantiles transform those exact probabilities. PHP’s sampled points must match at 1e-15 + 1e-12*abs(reference); discrete values match the integer quantiles. The full output is consumed by mean/variance calculations and checked against theoretical moments within eight standard errors (using the distribution’s fourth central moment for variance). Fixed seeds make these checks deterministic.
This complements the ordinary 25-case independent stream/quantile fixture suite. It does not compare every element to R and does not claim that R’s own RNG shares the ChaCha sequence. Each timed result undergoes the same numerical checks again.

Timing interpretation
Five measurements follow one untimed warm-up. Timing includes ChaCha setup, quantile evaluation, PHP result allocation and ordinary reclamation of previous results. JSON I/O and numerical summaries are outside the timed call. Peak RSS covers the whole worker, including summaries and inputs; it is not isolated RNG state memory. title: Published mixed-model verification data: provenance
text:
Sleep deprivation
sleepstudy.csv contains reaction times in milliseconds over ten days for eighteen subjects. All 180 rows are retained. Our verification model uses a fixed intercept, Days and a random intercept by Subject. The lme4 dataset documentation attributes the data to Belenky et al. (2003). Its example uses random slopes; our chosen random-intercept comparison is a different, deliberately simpler model.

title: Published mixed-model verification data: provenance
text:
Orthodontic growth
Orthodont.csv contains 108 measurements from 27 children. We use age, an explicitly constructed female indicator and age × female, with a random intercept by Subject. All observations and original columns are retained. Female=1 for Sex equal to ‘Female’; Male is the reference category. The nlme dataset documentation describes the measurements and cites Potthoff and Roy (1964), and Pinheiro and Bates (2000), Appendix A.17.

title: Published mixed-model verification data: provenance
text:
Worker and machine productivity
Machines.csv contains 54 observations: six workers each operated three machine brands three times. We construct separate B and C indicators, with A as the reference brand, and a random intercept by Worker. All rows and original columns are retained. This comparison has no worker-by-machine random interaction. The nlme documentation cites Milliken and Johnson (1992), and Pinheiro and Bates (2000), Appendix A.14.

title: Published mixed-model verification data: provenance
text:
High School and Beyond
Hsb82.csv contains all 7,185 observations in the package’s 1982 High School and Beyond sample. We retain the five columns used by the model: school, individual SES, school mean SES, school sector and mathematics achievement. The fixed columns are intercept, SES, mean SES and Catholic=1 for sector equal to ‘Catholic’; Public is the reference. School is the grouping variable, with 160 schools and 14–67 students per school. The mlmRev reference manual describes the data and cites Raudenbush and Bryk (2002), chapter 4.

title: Published mixed-model verification data: provenance
text:
Snapshot and model construction
The exporter tests/export-lmm-public-data.R reads installed package data and writes UTF-8 CSVs with original row order and no row-name column. The fixture generator tests/generate-lmm-public-fixtures.py constructs the numeric designs listed above, maps first-appearance group labels to integer core IDs, and saves lme4 and nlme ML reference outputs. The PHP verification also exercises original string labels. No rows are sampled or silently removed. The matrix-building code is an explicit test helper; the native API still accepts vanilla arrays and adds no categorical encoder or formula parser.
The snapshots are distributed from packages declaring GPL (>= 2); package source links and study citations are in sources.json, and COPYING contains GPL version 2. These package distribution notices do not claim new ownership of the original studies. R and these data packages are development dependencies.
To intentionally refresh snapshots and expectations:
Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("lme4", "nlme", "mlmRev"), repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")'
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/generate-lmm-public-fixtures.py --export
To regenerate expectations from the existing, checksum-verified snapshots, omit --export; only lme4 and nlme are needed in R. Review CSVs, sources.json, tests/fixtures/lmm-public-r.json and the executed comparison together. A changed source snapshot must never be accepted solely by changing its hash.

title: Descriptive statistics
text: These ten functions summarize ordinary PHP numeric arrays. They are deterministic, stateless native calculations; no intercept, model fitting or retained sample object is involved. Array keys are ignored and iteration order aligns pairs and weights. Results are floats except stat_quantile_array, which returns a packed list in probability-array iteration order.

title: Descriptive statistics
Descriptive statistics
text:
Weight definitions
Let \(W=\sum_i w_i\), \(m=\sum_i w_i x_i/W\), and \(SS=\sum_i w_i(x_i-m)^2\). Weights must be nonnegative and finite; the retained total must be positive.








Weighted variance type
Definition
Interpretation




frequency (default)
\(SS/(W-1)\)
Replication/count weights; requires W > 1


reliability
\(SS/(W-\sum_i w_i^2/W)\)
Reliability/precision weights; requires a positive denominator


population
\(SS/W\)
Weighted population second moment



Frequency and reliability weighting differ. Integer frequency weights reproduce the sample variance of an expanded sample. Reliability/population results are invariant to multiplying all weights by a positive constant. Zero weights are allowed. One effective value has zero population variance but undefined reliability variance. Negative weights are rejected even when the paired value is missing. Weights are aligned to original input positions before pairwise deletion. The separate draw moments API always normalizes weights and calls reliability normalization 'unbiased'; it never treats weights as counts.

title: Descriptive statistics
text:
Missing values and errors
Null and NAN are missing values. The default missing: 'raise' rejects them with 1001. missing: 'drop' explicitly removes them, pairwise for covariance, correlation and weighted functions. No warning or retained-row metadata is returned; dropping is opt-in. Infinity always raises 1003, including an element paired with a missing value. Strings, booleans, objects and nested arrays raise 1001. All aligned arrays must have equal original lengths, or 1002 is raised.
Unsupported type/missing options, insufficient retained values, invalid weights or invalid probability domains raise 1001. NAN probability raises 1003. Nonfinite arithmetic results also raise 1003, including an overflowing weight sum or squared deviation. The explicit NAN for constant-input correlation remains valid. This release fixed a case where an overflowing variance had been hidden as zero by floating-point max(NAN, 0).
Sums use Neumaier compensation; variances/covariances use corrected two-pass centered moments. This improves accuracy with large common offsets. These are binary64 calculations and do not promise arbitrary-scale extended precision.

title: Descriptive statistics
text:
Example and verification
$values = [2.5, 3.1, 4.7, 1.2, 9.8, 5.5, 3.3];
$mean = Phit\stat_mean($values);                     // 4.3
$sampleVariance = Phit\stat_var($values);       // About 7.85667
$quartiles = Phit\stat_quantile_array($values, [.25, .5, .75]);
$explicitDrop = Phit\stat_mean([1, null, 3], missing: 'drop'); // 2
tests/descriptive.php checks 145 R reference quantities plus scalar/batch consistency, missing policies, pairwise deletion, weights, boundaries, malformed inputs and arithmetic overflow. crates/stats-core/tests/descriptive.rs checks the same stored R cases independently of PHP and adds core failure/degeneracy checks. The eight univariate samples, three paired samples and two weighted samples include large offsets, tiny values, constant data and reproducible simulations. Reference tolerance is relative 1e-12, with exact zeros. R is not required by the ordinary test suites.
Regenerate intentionally with Rscript tests/generate-distribution-fixtures.R; this also regenerates the distribution R fixture. The provenance manifest records inputs, versions, generators and hashes. The release gate includes the PHP suite and the runnable examples/distributions.php.

title: Development
text: This page is for working on phit itself: building from a checkout, running the tests, and changing the implementation. To use phit in an application, see Installation. Run the commands below from the repository root, which holds Cargo.toml, crates/ and examples/.

title: Development
text:
Environment
Following the official ext-php-rs installation guide and Hello World build workflow:
# macOS: Xcode command-line tools, Rust, PHP (includes headers), libclang
xcode-select --install
brew install rust php llvm
export PHP="$(brew --prefix php)/bin/php"
export PHP_CONFIG="$(brew --prefix php)/bin/php-config"
export PATH="$(brew --prefix php)/bin:$PATH"
# If bindgen cannot find libclang:
export LIBCLANG_PATH="$(brew --prefix llvm)/lib"
Linux (Debian or Ubuntu with PHP 8.3, 8.4 or 8.5 in the configured repositories):
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install build-essential clang libclang-dev php-cli php-dev curl
# Install stable Rust using https://rustup.rs, then source ~/.cargo/env.
export PHP="$(command -v php)"
export PHP_CONFIG="$(command -v php-config)"
Check php -v, php-config --version, and rustc --version. PHP and php-config must belong to the same installation (including architecture, ZTS/NTS and debug mode). scripts/check and scripts/check-fpm take PHP from php-config --php-binary unless PHP is set, so a different php earlier on PATH, such as Herd’s, does not matter to them. Commands you run by hand still need the matching php. The macOS linker configuration permits symbols resolved by PHP when it loads the extension; Linux needs no macOS linker flags.
When using Homebrew LLVM’s libclang on macOS, select the matching compiler and builtin header directory as well. Mixing Xcode’s older arm_neon.h with a newer libclang can fail before any statistical tests run:
export LIBCLANG_PATH="$(brew --prefix llvm)/lib"
export CC="$(brew --prefix llvm)/bin/clang"
export CXX="$(brew --prefix llvm)/bin/clang++"
export BINDGEN_EXTRA_CLANG_ARGS="-resource-dir=$($CC -print-resource-dir) -isysroot=$(xcrun --show-sdk-path)"
The CI matrix disables fail-fast so a macOS failure does not cancel Linux evidence.

title: Development
text:
Build and run
Run from the repository root with the environment above:
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo build -p phit --locked
# macOS:
export STATS_EXTENSION="$PWD/target/debug/libphit.dylib"
# Linux instead:
# export STATS_EXTENSION="$PWD/target/debug/libphit.so"
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" -m
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" -r 'echo phpversion("phit"), PHP_EOL;'

Installation covers PIE and the prebuilt binaries. Deploying to servers covers containers and PHP-FPM, and Releasing covers release artifacts.

title: Development
text:
Numerical dependency policy
The engine uses nalgebra’s Rust-native SVD and QR. There is one maintained numerical path, with no BLAS/LAPACK dependency or backend selection. We defer external numerical backends until a concrete requirement justifies the additional build and deployment work. The earlier Accelerate trial is retained as historical benchmark evidence; its Cargo feature and foreign-call wrapper have been removed.
The posterior-draw kernels also use nalgebra Cholesky, triangular solves and pivoted LU. Their numerical notes document covariance/rank tolerances and independent fixtures; tests/draws.php is included in scripts/check.

title: Development
text:
Changing the implementation
Keep statistical calculations in crates/stats-core and PHP conversion in crates/php-extension. Work in small increments with established numerical crates. Check APIs against the dependency versions in Cargo.lock. Explain important mathematical steps near the code, and update contracts and reference tests when behavior changes. Do not add abstractions for hypothetical models.
Follow verification.qmd for the checks appropriate to a change. The tested baseline is Apple Silicon, Rust 1.99 and Homebrew PHP 8.5.10. CI runs the checks on macOS and Ubuntu, and the packaging workflow tests Linux x86_64 and aarch64 at PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5.
The general mixed fitter also uses pinned Rust-native bobyqa and argmin (Nelder–Mead). These add no C/Fortran, BLAS or LAPACK runtime requirements. See R compatibility for reference regeneration and the remaining native optimizer backend work.
./scripts/check runs the complete offline gate: Rust tests and clippy, every PHP suite and example, the stub and signature checks, the reference manifest, and the site export. Run it before pushing.

title: Building and maintaining the documentation
text: All documentation sources in docs/ use Quarto .qmd, including executable estimator walkthroughs. The root README.md remains a short repository entry point. docs/_quarto.yml defines a searchable HTML website with navigation, mathematical notation, code and results. Quarto builds into the gitignored docs/_site/ directory. scripts/render-docs copies the rendered website into docs/ alongside the .qmd sources, including docs/index.html and required assets. The statistical engine does not depend on Quarto.

title: Building and maintaining the documentation
text:
Render or preview saved results
Install the Quarto CLI for your platform. On macOS, brew install --cask quarto is also available. Check quarto --version; this project was rendered with Quarto 1.10.18.
From the repository root:
quarto render docs
quarto preview docs
The website reuses saved computations in docs/_freeze/. Keep this directory in version control: a complete website render does not require Python, R, or a built PHP extension when those saved results are present. The JSON comparison report, reference fixtures and executable source code are also retained in the repository. Generated HTML/assets are checked in for GitHub Pages; .qmd files remain the editable sources. Quarto’s local .quarto/ state stays gitignored.
A render that reuses saved outputs is a presentation check, not a fresh numerical verification. The walkthroughs show versions from their last execution. Quarto’s freeze documentation explains why incremental file renders execute code even when a project-wide render reuses outputs.

title: Building and maintaining the documentation
text:
Recompute the walkthroughs
Follow development setup to select matching PHP and headers, and install R with Rscript available. The mixed-model reference also requires R’s lme4 package, plus nlme for the published-data comparison. These are development dependencies rather than PHP runtime dependencies:
Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("lme4", "nlme"), repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")'
From the repository root:
python3 -m venv .context/notebooks-venv
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/pip install -r docs/notebooks/requirements.txt
export QUARTO_PYTHON="$PWD/.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python"
# macOS development installation; select matching paths on your platform.
export PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php
export PHP_CONFIG=/opt/homebrew/bin/php-config
cargo build -p phit --locked
export STATS_EXTENSION="$PWD/target/debug/libphit.dylib"
# Linux: use libphit.so and matching PHP/PHP_CONFIG paths.
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_ols.py
quarto render docs/notebooks/ols-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/ols-verification.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/lmm-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/lmm-verification.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/lmm-public-verification.qmd
quarto render docs/data/lmm/index.qmd
quarto render docs/benchmarks/lmm.qmd
quarto render docs
The individual page renders execute their code and refresh the saved outputs; the final full render assembles the website. RSCRIPT can select a non-default Rscript executable. QUARTO_PYTHON selects the virtual environment without adding machine-specific paths to the project configuration. Review changes to .qmd, _freeze/ and verifications/ols-results.json together. Input-data or estimator changes require re-execution even if the prose has not changed.

title: Building and maintaining the documentation
text:
Recompute each model’s notebooks
With the environment above, each estimator’s comparison script and notebooks run in this order:
export QUARTO_PYTHON="$PWD/.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python"
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_ols.py
quarto render docs/notebooks/ols-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/ols-verification.qmd
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_logistic.py
quarto render docs/notebooks/logistic-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/logistic-verification.qmd
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_probit.py
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_poisson.py
quarto render docs/notebooks/probit-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/probit-verification.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/poisson-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/poisson-verification.qmd
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_lmm.py
quarto render docs/notebooks/lmm-math.qmd
quarto render docs/notebooks/lmm-verification.qmd
quarto render docs
The individual page renders execute all chunks in order and update _freeze/. Review source, output and comparison-report diffs when regenerating. Outputs record evidence from the environment used, not a guarantee for every platform. The verification scripts capture PHP warnings to keep JSON output valid, then show and check those warnings explicitly. Use a Quarto-compatible editor for interactive .qmd authoring; generated .ipynb files are not the maintained source.

title: Building and maintaining the documentation
text:
Writing a walkthrough
Each implemented estimator has an executable walkthrough. Do not create placeholder notebooks for methods phit does not implement.
Use a small reproducible simulated dataset with named variables, units, noise, and meaningful relationships. State its generating equation, seed, population parameters, and observed sample correlations. Save and share the actual observations; label them synthetic and explain that correlation alone is not causation. See the learning-data convention. State the model assumptions and input ordering, derive the calculations before displaying them, connect fields to production code, and explain edge cases. Supply equivalent R, statsmodels and PHP calls when those references support the estimator. State any differences in statistical conventions rather than silently adapting one library’s results. Keep assertions near the results and preserve executed outputs. Share inputs with reference tests where possible; avoid three separate datasets that only look similar.

title: Building and maintaining the documentation
text:
Authoring and verification
Edit .qmd files directly. Ordinary fenced blocks such as python, r and php are displayed examples; {python} chunks execute in the Jupyter kernel. Both OLS walkthroughs use Python chunks, with the comparison runner invoking R and PHP. Execution starts in docs/ and the code discovers the repository root by locating Cargo.toml. A missing dependency or failed assertion must fail the render.
Use relative links to .qmd pages so Quarto rewrites them to HTML links. Keep local reference data and scripts alongside the verification document. Each future implemented estimator should have a derivation walkthrough and equivalent-model verification evidence, following the notebook guide.
For prose-only pages, render the site and check navigation and local links. Any edit to a computational walkthrough (including prose) requires an individual page render to update its frozen content. For computational edits, rerun the affected pages and comparison scripts, inspect output, and run the appropriate Rust/PHP checks. Saved results must never be mistaken for a new estimator test run.

title: Building and maintaining the documentation
text:
Standard figures
All benchmark and notebook figures use the shared R/ggplot2 strategy in Figure conventions. SVG/PNG exports, fixed language ordering, colors/shapes, units, scale choices and input/package provenance use the same renderer. Python remains a numerical/verification notebook engine rather than a second drawing implementation. Matplotlib is not a documentation dependency.
To refresh saved figures without estimating or timing anything:
Rscript docs/figures/render.R --all
./scripts/render-docs
The renderer uses saved reports and small notebook-exported point snapshots. Individual .qmd execution invokes the R renderer when appropriate. Saved images and frozen outputs support browsing/rendering without rerunning scientific checks.

title: Building and maintaining the documentation
text:
Publish
phpstats.org imports the rendered HTML committed under docs/, and GitHub Pages serves the same directory at https://phpstats.github.io/phit/. Neither runs Quarto. The site’s navigation is the sidebar in docs/_quarto.yml, so every page listed there needs its rendered HTML committed. After editing .qmd sources or refreshing frozen results, run:
./scripts/render-docs
Commit the regenerated HTML/assets with their sources and push to main. docs/.nojekyll lets GitHub Pages serve the static Quarto website directly, including asset directories containing underscores. quarto render docs alone writes only docs/_site/; the script also copies the result into docs/.

title: Extension or polyfill
text:
phit has two implementations of the same Phit\ functions:
Code written against one runs unchanged on the other. Each polyfill release reproduces one phit release. Polyfill 0.3.0 reproduces phit v0.3.0, 0.2.0 reproduces v0.2.0, and 0.1.0 reproduces v0.1.1.

title: Extension or polyfill
text:
How they coexist
Composer loads the polyfill’s bootstrap.php through its files autoload. If extension_loaded('phit') is true, the bootstrap returns before defining anything, so every Phit\ function is the extension’s. Installing both is therefore safe: the extension is used where it is loaded, and the polyfill everywhere else, such as a CI runner or a host where extensions cannot be installed.
The polyfill does not fill gaps in an older extension. If the loaded extension is older than the polyfill’s phit release, the functions added since then stay undefined.
The polyfill’s composer.json declares "provide": {"ext-phit": "*"}. A package that requires ext-phit is therefore satisfied by the polyfill, including one that uses the functions the polyfill lacks.

title: Extension or polyfill
text:
What the polyfill covers
The polyfill provides 232 of phit 0.3.0’s 233 functions. It does not provide Phit\read_csv() or the Phit\CsvReader class. Without the extension, function_exists('Phit\read_csv') and class_exists('Phit\CsvReader') return false, and Phit\Polyfill::supports('Phit\read_csv') returns false.







Area
Polyfill




Formula models and prediction
model_matrix, fit_lm, fit_glm, fit_lmer, fit_glmer and predict, with a port of the extension’s formula parser


Matrix models
All seven fit_* matrix functions


Mixed models
The same structures as the extension: fit_lmer with random intercepts and slopes, (x || g), several terms and nesting, by REML or ML with BOBYQA or Nelder–Mead; fit_glmer with one binomial logit (1 | g), by Laplace or adaptive quadrature with up to 61 points


Distributions, descriptive statistics, seeded sampling
All functions


Posterior-draw kernels
draws_moments, draws_covariance_map and draws_affine


CSV input
Not provided; phibble’s DataFrame::fromCsv() falls back to its own PHP reader



The polyfill’s test suite runs the extension’s reference fixtures, including the lme4 and seeded-sampling references, at the extension’s tolerances. Randomized parity tests compare its results with the extension’s. In those tests the posterior-draw kernels and the random-intercept and random-slope fits are bit-identical.

title: Extension or polyfill
text:
Differences

The listwise-deletion warning is E_USER_WARNING in the polyfill and E_WARNING in the extension. The text is the same.
Arguments of the wrong scalar type follow PHP’s userland rules in the polyfill: coercion, or a TypeError under strict_types.
Every polyfill function throws an exception with code 1007 while OPcache’s JIT is compiling the process. The JIT has produced wrong numerical results in the polyfill, so the polyfill refuses to run under it. PHP 8.4 and 8.5 disable the JIT by default. PHP 8.3’s default settings (opcache.jit=tracing with opcache.jit_buffer_size=0) also leave it off. The extension runs under any JIT setting.
On an x86-64 CPU without fused multiply-add, the extension’s products of matrices larger than 5×5 can differ from the polyfill’s in the last bit.

title: Extension or polyfill
text:
Speed
The polyfill is slower, and the gap grows with model size. These timings were recorded on an Apple M5 Ultra with PHP 8.5.10, OPcache on and the JIT off.










Fit
Recorded
Polyfill
Extension
Ratio




fit_ols, n = 100,000, 10 predictors
2026-10-28, polyfill ab803fd, phit 3861d77
262 ms

9.1×


fit_logistic, same design
2026-10-28, polyfill ab803fd, phit 3861d77

Mixed models ran 13 to 78 times slower in that comparison. The polyfill’s cost grows with roughly the cube of the number of random coefficients.

title: Extension or polyfill
text:
Versions and platforms
The polyfill’s composer.json requires PHP ^8.3. Its CI tests PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 on Linux, in five OPcache and JIT modes, and on macOS in two. Windows is untested. The extension supports PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 on Linux and macOS.
The polyfill’s own documentation is in the phit-polyfill repository.

title: A first model
text: This page fits a linear model to a small table of flats, reads the estimates, and predicts rents for flats that are not in the table. It assumes the extension is installed.

title: A first model
A first model
A first model
text:
Read the result
The result is a plain PHP array. Every coefficient list follows the order of columns.
foreach ($fit['columns'] as $i => $name) {
    printf("%-14s %9.2f %8.2f %7.4f  [%8.2f, %8.2f]\n", $name, $fit['coefficients'][$i],
        $fit['std_errors'][$i], $fit['p_values'][$i], ...$fit['conf_int'][$i]);
}
(Intercept)       352.64   179.87  0.0976  [  -87.49,   792.77]
area               19.18     3.23  0.0010  [   11.27,    27.09]
districtnorth     203.64   151.14  0.2265  [ -166.19,   573.47]
districtsouth     232.16   119.64  0.1004  [  -60.58,   524.90]
Each additional square meter adds about 19 to the expected rent. The district coefficients are differences from east.







Key
Contents




columns, named
Coefficient names, and a name => coefficient map


coefficients, std_errors, t_statistics, p_values
One value per column


conf_int
95% intervals, [lower, upper] per column


covariance
The coefficient covariance matrix


fitted, residuals
One value per retained row


r_squared, adj_r_squared, sigma, rss, log_likelihood, df_residual
Fit statistics


n_input, n_observations, n_dropped, retained_rows, dropped_rows
Sample accounting


diagnostics
Solver, convergence and warnings



printf("R-squared %.4f, sigma %.2f, %d residual df, %d of %d rows\n",
    $fit['r_squared'], $fit['sigma'], $fit['df_residual'], $fit['n_observations'], $fit['n_input']);
echo json_encode($fit['diagnostics']), "\n";
R-squared 0.9270, sigma 146.29, 6 residual df, 10 of 10 rows
{"converged":true,"solver":"scaled_svd","warnings":[]}
fit_glm, fit_lmer and fit_glmer return the same naming and accounting keys, with the statistics of their model. Linear and generalized linear models and mixed models list them.

title: A first model
A first model
text:
Missing values
null and NAN are missing. By default, a row with a missing value in any column the formula uses is dropped, and the fit emits one E_WARNING. With rent set to null in the third row:
Warning: Phit\fit_lm(): Phit\fit_lm dropped 1 of 10 observations with missing values (listwise deletion)
The result then reports n_observations 9, n_input 10 and dropped_rows [2], and diagnostics.warnings holds the same notice. Pass missing: 'raise' to reject missing values instead. The call then throws an Exception with code 1001 and the message missing values found with missing='raise'. Missing data defines which values count as missing and how rows are counted.

title: A first model
text:
Errors
Invalid input and failed fits throw a PHP Exception. Its getCode() gives the category: 1001 for invalid input, 1002 for mismatched lengths, 1004 for a rank-deficient design, 1006 for nonconvergence, and so on. The full table is in the API overview.

title: Installation
text: phit is a PHP extension. It is installed into PHP itself, once per PHP installation, rather than into a project with Composer. Projects that cannot install extensions can use the polyfill instead.

title: Installation
text:
Requirements

PHP 8.3, 8.4 or 8.5, non-thread-safe (NTS). Thread-safe (ZTS) builds are not supported.
Linux or macOS. Windows is not supported.
PIE, PHP’s extension installer, for the standard installation.

PIE builds the extension from source, so the machine also needs:

PHP’s development files: phpize and php-config for the same PHP installation.
A C toolchain with autoconf and make.
Rust, stable, from rustup.
Clang and libclang.

These build tools are not needed at runtime. The prebuilt Linux binaries need none of them.

title: Installation
text:
Install with PIE
pie install phpstats/phit
PIE downloads the latest release from Packagist, builds it, copies phit.so into the extension directory, and enables it for the PHP it runs under. To choose another PHP installation, pass --with-php-config=/path/to/php-config.
On Debian or Ubuntu, the build tools come from:
sudo apt-get install build-essential autoconf pkg-config clang libclang-dev php-dev
curl -fsSL https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y
Installing v0.3.0 this way was tested in a Debian Bookworm container with the official php:8.4-cli-bookworm image, PIE 1.5.0 and stable Rust. The image provides PHP’s development files, and the test added Clang, libclang and the image’s $PHPIZE_DEPS.
On macOS, install the Xcode command-line tools (xcode-select --install), Rust from rustup, and PHP and autoconf from Homebrew (brew install php autoconf). pie build phpstats/phit completed for v0.3.0 on macOS 27 (Apple silicon) with Homebrew PHP 8.5. If the build cannot find libclang, the development guide shows the variables that select Homebrew’s LLVM.

Prebuilt Linux binaries
Each GitHub release has tested binaries for Debian Bookworm (glibc), NTS, non-debug PHP:
