The reference manifest indexes software versions actually recorded in fixtures, generators and their hashes, input hashes, model/options sources, compared quantities and tolerance policies. It does not invent missing historical package versions or represent old outputs as regenerated. Fixture values and test sources remain authoritative. Older fixed-model fixtures record R’s version; generator code records family, formula, seed and controls.

title: v0.1 stabilization and release assessment
text:
Correctness fixes and compatibility notes

Single-level logistic/probit now canonicalize accepted integer successes to round(y*trials)/trials, matching the mixed fitter. Count tolerance is 1e-8. Tiny encoded values cannot create fictitious events; all-failure/all-success data still fail. Response residuals use canonical proportions.
Every binomial interface now enforces the previously mixed-only limit of 1,000,000 trials per row, including original rows subsequently dropped. This is a deliberate validation tightening: larger-count binomial likelihood arithmetic has not been independently verified.
OLS rejects nonzero residuals whose squared norm/variance underflows, rather than returning RSS=0 and an infinite perfect-fit likelihood. Exact zero residuals retain the documented infinity/undefined-inference convention. Overflowed total/weighted fitted variation now fails explicitly instead of leaking a spurious undefined R²; this was reproduced with weighted outcomes around 10^155.
GLMs preserve their ordinary zero-coefficient start. For extreme offsets (absolute logit/Poisson offset >20, probit >8) or Poisson counts >10^8, an explicit ones column enables a finite marginal intercept fallback. Poisson intercept/exposure arithmetic uses log-sum-exp. Tests include constant offsets ±1,000. This does not establish arbitrary extreme heterogeneous-offset support.
Poisson log masses for counts at least 16 use deviance plus Stirling error, avoiding cancellation between large factorial/log-mean terms. Counts of 10^12 are checked against R; deviance keeps its existing expm1 calculation.
Binomial final LL/deviance/AIC receive explicit range checks. Only rounding-level negative deviance is rounded to zero; a larger violation of saturated likelihood fails.
Rust errors now carry ErrorKind; PHP retains the Exception class and adds stable codes 1001–1008. Rust .0 still exposes the message; direct tuple construction changes to StatsError::new(kind, message).
Successful result arrays gain diagnostics; existing top-level keys and PHP signatures/defaults remain. Strict consumers must allow the additional key. Missing-row warnings are still emitted once and also recorded in diagnostics. The two internal PHP-boundary expect calls were removed. ext-php-rs’s handler catches Rust unwinding panics, but allocation failure/process abort is not recoverable; no memory-safety guarantee is inferred from ordinary unit tests.

See diagnostic/error definitions.

title: v0.1 stabilization and release assessment
text:
Stress tests and numerical limits
tests/fixtures/stress-r.json records each design, response, weight, offset, reference specification, R version and tolerance. It tests near collinearity, columns in different units, outcomes scaled by 10^-140 and 10^140, tiny positive residual variance, weighted/no-intercept estimation, rare outcomes, ±1,000 constant offsets, sparse Poisson outcomes and 10^12 counts. Known ±1,000 binary predictors with balanced non-extreme observations remain valid (R saturation warnings are recorded), and a no-intercept Poisson model tests known means down to exp(-500).
Absolute tolerances are expressed in response units: for scaled OLS estimates, SE/CI/fits/residuals they multiply response_scale, and for covariance its square. Dimensionless statistics and log likelihood are not rescaled. This avoids requiring relative accuracy in covariance entries whose mathematical value is zero. The nearly collinear fixture uses a disclosed 1e-6 relative tolerance; this does not relax the original, well-conditioned reference suite.
Existing tests retain exact rank deficiency, complete/quasi separation, nonfinite and invalid inputs, zero/invalid weights, exhausted budgets, legitimate variance boundaries, correlated slopes, nested/crossed and four-level Gaussian designs, ML/REML, predictor-unit invariance, and quadrature tail-weight stability. The new dense-limit test rejects q=513 before factorization.
Limitations remain:

Numerical inputs become f64, with a 53-bit significand. Integer-valued inputs beyond 2^53 can lose exactness during PHP-to-Rust conversion; arbitrary-precision count/design arithmetic is not supported. The stress checks do not establish accuracy for every representable count or input magnitude.
Full rank at floating-point precision does not imply well-conditioned inference. Separation detection is a direction certificate, not a complete linear-programming proof. Finite uncertain estimates can be valid; difficult problems may fail rank, line-search, arithmetic or iteration checks.
General Gaussian computation is dense: q≤512 and n(q+p+1)≤50,000,000, excluding additional temporary matrices and PHP arrays. These are guards, not a memory reservation or sparse-solver capability. No new general-mixed performance claim is inferred from the fast specialization.
General Gaussian convergence uses native optimizer termination/bounds and finite factors/outputs. A final gradient/Hessian convergence audit of variance parameters is not implemented; diagnostics do not fabricate one. Multi-start global optimality is not established. Use reference comparisons and start/optimizer sensitivity for difficult fits.
Gaussian inference uses plug-in GLS covariance and normal Wald tests, not Satterthwaite/Kenward–Roger corrections. REML criteria depend on the fixed design and should not compare models with different fixed-effect columns.
Logistic mixed inference uses joint observed information of the chosen approximate likelihood. Its score gate and positive Hessian are numerical checks, not approximation-accuracy proofs. Tau≤20, scaled beta bounds±100, one grouping term, integer trials and max61 AGQ remain explicit limits.
In the rare-event fixture, Laplace estimates group SD≈7.30 while 61 nodes give ≈3.36. Agreement with lme4 at one node does not establish accuracy. The integration notebook retains the independent error checks and explains grouped-binomial likelihood constants.
Missing values use listwise deletion; this is a data policy, not an assumption that missingness is ignorable or that deletion produces unbiased inference.

title: v0.1 stabilization and release assessment
text:
PHP contract gate
stubs/php-stats.php is for IDE/static-analysis indexing, not runtime inclusion. Generate it with the extension loaded:
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" scripts/php-stubs.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" scripts/php-stubs.php --check
The generator reads actual native argument types/names/defaults via Reflection. tests/fixtures/php-api.json freezes those signatures and expected result keys; tests/stability.php fits every estimator and checks result keys and diagnostic aliases. Updating the API fixture requires an explicit --write-api, which should only follow compatibility review. Structured PHPDoc documents matrix vectors, group types, random terms and per-function return shapes. ext-php-rs also offers its official cargo-php stub workflow; our maintained declarations additionally include result-array shapes.

title: v0.1 stabilization and release assessment
text:
Performance preservation
The saved pre-audit binary was compared with the stabilized binary using the same inputs, runtime, five complete timed fits after warm-up, and single-thread environment. Every numerical comparison passed. Timings include PHP input conversion and full result materialization; JSON serialization is outside timed fitting. Whole-process RSS includes runtime/startup/serialization. There is one local measurement batch, so small percentage differences in millisecond fits are not evidence of regressions or speed improvements. No matrix backend or Gaussian square-root path was replaced.
Targeted investigation caught a 100,000-row Poisson regression during this pass: an unconditional marginal-intercept start took 61 iterations instead of six, with negligible estimate differences but a roughly 16-fold slowdown. It was restricted to extreme inputs where the zero start is unsafe. The final report also records iteration/evaluation counts. This preserves the existing ordinary iteration path and avoids treating a theoretically helpful start as an optimization.

title: v0.1 stabilization and release assessment
text:
Release readiness and remaining gates
The native functions, offline statistical suite and examples work on the tested macOS/PHP combination. This is a release candidate, not a claim of universal production readiness and not a published release.
Before distribution:

Run the new CI on Linux and macOS and record results; exercise each PHP/SAPI, architecture and ZTS/NTS combination advertised as supported. PHP 8.3+ is the intended consumer range, but this pass executed PHP 8.5.10 CLI only.
Preserve the root MIT LICENSE and the separate notices/provenance for bundled reference data and third-party assets when preparing distribution packages.
Review diagnostics, input tightening and the retained numerical limits against application requirements. Confirm FPM headers/build ABI and restart workers after installation; a CLI load does not verify web-server deployment.
Choose release metadata/distribution packaging and publish through the project’s release workflow. This pass does not create a tag, commit, push or package release.

No full R/lme4 compatibility promise is made. New families, inference methods, sparse general mixed computation and broader GLMM designs are outside this pass.

title: v0.1 stabilization and release assessment
text:
Review follow-up
A subsequent source review found obsolete exclusions in the contracts page and three PHP validation paths that emitted uncoded Exception instances. Those paths now use the same typed 1001 code for out-of-range binomial outcomes, invalid Poisson counts and invalid group IDs. The group parser is shared rather than duplicated. Regression tests check codes for logistic/probit, both simple mixed calls and general Gaussian mixed grouping, including invalid values on rows that would otherwise be dropped. Statistical algorithms and public signatures are unchanged.
The first GitHub CI run failed during macOS binding generation with incompatible Clang ARM builtin headers; Linux was cancelled by matrix fail-fast. The workflow now aligns Homebrew compiler, libclang and resource headers, and lets both platforms finish independently. This configuration change passes the full local gate with the aligned LLVM toolchain: 49 Rust tests, nine PHP suites and all seven examples. It still needs a successful remote run and is not Linux numerical verification. The original local validation record remains a dated snapshot.
An optional constrained first-order/curvature audit for general Gaussian variance parameters remains future work. Optimizer termination and verified stationarity are distinct; the current contract does not claim the latter. No strict stationarity option, prediction-only interface or new model family is introduced in this follow-up.

title: Verification
text: This page lists the checks that run on every change, the reference results they compare against, and their tolerances. Running them needs the build environment described in Development.

title: Verification
text:
Routine checks
From the repository root:
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo build -p phit --locked
# macOS; use libphit.so on Linux
export STATS_EXTENSION="$PWD/target/debug/libphit.dylib"
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" -m
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" -r 'echo phpversion("phit"), PHP_EOL;'
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/ols.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/logistic.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/ols.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" examples/logistic.php
cargo test verifies the independent Rust engine. The extension crate disables its Rust test harness; explicitly building it and running PHP integration tests are separate required checks for binding changes. For a release/deployment check, build with –release and run the PHP scripts against target/release instead. For documentation-only changes, check links, commands and claims against source; rerun numerical tests when behavior or implementation changes.

title: Verification
text:
Probability and descriptive APIs
The offline release gate runs tests/distributions.php, tests/descriptive.php and examples/distributions.php, along with the Rust distribution/descriptive suites. Distribution checks include 8,618 reference comparisons, 25 independent mpmath adjudications and 43 documented boundary differences. Descriptive tests add 145 R quantities, type-7 scalar/batch identities, strict/explicit-drop missing policies, pairwise alignment, weight definitions and arithmetic overflow errors. The distribution record describes provenance, reference limitations and operation-specific tolerances. The utility contract documents undefined correlation separately from numerical failure. tests/smoothing.php compares 15,639 density, bandwidth, interpolation, and ECDF quantities with R at relative 1e-12.
Refresh PHP error evidence without changing independent expected values:
PHP=/path/to/matching/php .context/v02/python/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_distributions.py --stored-references
python3 scripts/reference-manifest.py
python3 scripts/distribution-docs.py
Reference regeneration with R or 60-digit mpmath is intentional and separate; see the comparison page. Distribution scalar/batch/Rust/R/SciPy benchmarks and the seven-model pre-v0.2 preservation comparison run separately from the gate, with numerical agreement recorded before distribution timings. Seeded sampling adds 25 independently generated Python/R cases: 2,000 Rust engine/quantile values and 1,616 PHP transformed references, plus repeatability, prefix, state-isolation, domain/limit and moment checks. tests/rng.php and examples/rng.php run in the release gate. The readiness assessment records remaining release steps.

title: Verification
text:
Posterior-draw kernels
The release gate includes crates/stats-core/tests/draws.rs and tests/draws.php. Both consume 25 independent 80-digit Python Decimal cases, including covariance-map identities, affine round trips and log determinants. Strict validation includes zero weights, one effective draw and singular covariance, with explicit failures for map/affine numerical singularity. Provenance, formulas, numerical tolerances, reproduction commands and limitations are recorded in draw numerical notes. The benchmark validates complete outputs against R before recording timings; it runs separately from the offline release gate.

title: Verification
text:
PHP intercept and offset contracts
tests/intercept.php checks all seven PHP fitters with predictors-only inputs against the same complete design passed with intercept: false. Those results must be identical, including covariance, likelihood, group effects, row accounting, and diagnostics. Existing fixtures retain their literal matrices and their PHP runners explicitly opt out of insertion. No-intercept and intercept-only models are exercised separately; automatic insertion never changes random-design z.
Poisson exposure checks independently calculate the intercept-only weighted MLE, its standard error, likelihood and fitted counts. They use absolute tolerances 1e-10 for the coefficient/SE and 1e-9 for likelihood/counts. Rescaling exposure must shift only the intercept and preserve counts. Default-intercept weighted/offset fits also match stored R fixtures under the existing 1e-7 absolute + 1e-6 relative tolerance. Missing offsets participate in the same warning/deletion/strict-rejection contract as other inputs. The offline release gate includes this suite and the runnable exposure example.

title: Verification
text:
Reference and tolerances
tests/fixtures/ols-r.json contains deterministic results generated by base R 4.6.1 lm(), summary(), confint() and logLik(). R is not a runtime or test dependency. To regenerate: Rscript tests/generate-fixtures.R. The saved simulated housing observations in docs/data/housing.csv are shared by the PHP example, notebooks and one- and two-predictor reference fits. To regenerate that dataset intentionally, run Rscript tests/generate-learning-data.R first, then regenerate fixtures, the three-way report and both notebook outputs. The dataset generator specifies its RNG and seed; ordinary rendering and testing read the saved observations and do not generate fresh random samples. Rust and PHP tests compare noisy simple, multiple, no-intercept and correlated full-rank regressions, and include perfect/zero fits. Tolerance is 1e-9 + 1e-7 * abs(reference) for each compared quantity. Perfect fits compare coefficients, predictions, residuals and standard errors, but omit unstable t/p, R-squared and likelihood comparisons; Rust also compares finite confidence intervals. Zero-fit conventions are tested directly. R’s undefined quantities are stored as JSON null. Invalid shapes, insufficient observations and rank failure are tested separately because this implementation rejects cases that R may handle by dropping aliased coefficients.

For ordinary fixtures, comparisons include coefficients, covariance, fitted values, residuals, standard errors, t-statistics, p-values, confidence intervals, RSS, residual variance, sigma, R-squared, adjusted R-squared and likelihood. Residual degrees of freedom is also checked. This is a small deterministic suite, not proof of correctness for every floating-point input. CI runs it on Linux and macOS, and the packaging workflow runs it on Linux x86_64 and aarch64 at PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5, including a PHP-FPM request. It does not exercise extreme scales or every array-key pattern.

title: Verification
text:
Maintaining evidence
When changing an estimator or inference calculation, add a case that distinguishes the intended behavior from the old behavior. Compare against R where its conventions match ours, and test deliberate differences explicitly. Keep fixture inputs, generator and expected outputs together. Inspect regenerated fixture diffs; do not simply relax a tolerance to hide a discrepancy. When reporting verification, identify which Rust/PHP checks ran and which platform was used.
The current absolute-plus-relative tolerance supports near-zero quantities as well as larger ones. It does not establish relative accuracy for p-values much smaller than the absolute tolerance. If a change depends on extreme tails, add focused reference tests and a suitable tolerance for those values.

title: Verification
text:
Executed three-way evidence
The OLS verification report and verification notebook estimate the same cases afresh in R, Python statsmodels and PHP. Python/R are optional development tools; the ordinary Rust/PHP tests remain independent of them. The math notebook exposes each intermediate calculation. Follow notebook setup to regenerate the comparison report and saved notebook outputs. Each future implemented estimator should have a walkthrough and equivalent-model evidence where reference support exists.

title: Verification
text:
Scale and performance checks
The OLS benchmark report records release-extension timings, input loading, whole-process time and peak resident memory against R and statsmodels. Its standard cases include 1,000, 100,000 and one million observations with three coefficients, plus 100,000 observations with eleven coefficients (intercept included). It checks all inference and scalar statistics and ten sampled fitted/residual values against R; it does not compare every observation-length output on these large cases. These checks run separately from the small unit/reference suite.
Run .context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/benchmarks/run.py after building the release extension with matching PHP headers. Review raw results and numerical agreement before reporting speed comparisons. Follow the report for timing boundaries, backend settings, hardware, reproduction and evidence limitations.

title: Verification
text:
Binary logistic regression
tests/fixtures/logistic-r.json stores base R glm(..., family=binomial()) results for simulated students, one predictor, multiple predictors, no intercept, intercept only, highly correlated full-rank columns, and imbalanced outcomes. Regenerate intentionally with Rscript tests/generate-logistic-fixtures.R; this also regenerates the saved teaching observations in docs/data/learning.csv. Wald intervals use confint.default(), since glm’s ordinary confint() uses profile likelihood. Reference fitting uses epsilon 1e-14 to stabilize final information/covariance agreement.
Rust and PHP tests compare all statistical fields and full observation vectors with tolerance 1e-9 + 1e-7 × abs(reference). Rejection cases include malformed inputs, nonbinary outcomes, one retained class, rank deficiency, complete and quasi separation. Rust tests cover extreme logits and iteration exhaustion. PHP tests cover listwise deletion, warnings, row accounting, strict missingness and invalid values before deletion. Three-way verification also checks a sample with missing rows. These tests do not establish exhaustive separation detection.
PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php .context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_logistic.py
PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php .context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/benchmarks/run.py --model logistic
See the verification record, executed comparison and release benchmark.

title: Verification
text:
Probit and Poisson
tests/fixtures/probit-r.json and poisson-r.json are generated with base R glm, normal Wald inference and tolerance epsilon 1e-16. Regenerate intentionally with Rscript tests/generate-probit-poisson-fixtures.R; this also writes both shared teaching samples. Six fixtures per method cover named simulations, one predictor, multiple predictors, no intercept, intercept only, correlated columns and imbalanced/sparse outcomes. Three-way scripts add two missing rows and compare all fields/full observation vectors at 1e-9 + 1e-7 × abs(reference).
Probit comparisons use expected-information covariance in both reference libraries. Rust tests include underflowing normal log tails, failed convergence and separation. Poisson tests cover integer validation, zero counts, precision of near-zero deviance, failed convergence and selected boundary designs. PHP tests check missing warnings, strict policies, invalid outcomes before deletion, row alignment and convergence metadata. Existing OLS/logistic tests continue to cover shared binding conversion.
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/probit.php
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/poisson.php
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_probit.py
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_poisson.py
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/benchmarks/run.py --model probit
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/benchmarks/run.py --model poisson
See the probit comparison, Poisson comparison and their benchmark pages. These cases establish tested behavior, not exhaustive separation/boundary detection or coverage of Linux/PHP-FPM deployment.

title: Verification
text:
Gaussian random-intercept ML
tests/fixtures/lmm-r.json stores six lme4 ML fits: the simulated schools, one predictor, no intercept, intercept only, an additional singleton group and an exact zero-between-group-variance boundary. The generator Rscript tests/generate-lmm-fixtures.R intentionally refreshes both fixtures and docs/data/schools.csv. lme4 is a development dependency, never a runtime requirement. R uses REML=FALSE with bobyqa rhoend=1e-10.
Rust/PHP comparisons cover fixed coefficients, plug-in GLS covariance and Wald inference, population/conditional fitted values, both residual definitions, shrunken group effects, variance components, ICC, marginal likelihood and AIC. Tolerance is 1e-7 + 1e-6 × abs(reference), reflecting independently optimized variance components. A balanced intercept-only case also has independently known ML variance and shrinkage results. Tests reject invalid/unidentifiable samples and positive-residual-variance failures, and verify units/row order, exact boundary behavior, typed group IDs and listwise deletion across x/y/groups.
The three-way comparison uses statsmodels MixedLM ML estimates with the declared GLS covariance convention. Its exact zero-variance case uses a separately labeled NumPy OLS-limit check, since a statsmodels mixed optimizer is not a reliable exact-boundary reference. It also tests a sample with missing values in all three inputs. The stored report records the Python backend, warnings and covariance convention for each case.
php -n -d "extension=$STATS_EXTENSION" tests/lmm.php
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_lmm.py
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/benchmarks/run.py --model lmm
The finite profile search is not an exhaustive global-optimization proof. The original fast call remains one random intercept with Gaussian ML. The expanded general fitter now has separate REML/random-slope/multiple-term tests; finite-sample mixed-model inference adjustments remain open.

title: Verification
text:
Published Gaussian mixed-model data
The published-data comparison checks sleepstudy (180 observations), Orthodont (108), Machines (54) and Hsb82 (7,185) against R lme4, R nlme and Python statsmodels. Both R packages have saved expected outputs in tests/fixtures/lmm-public-r.json, checked by Rust and PHP without runtime R/Python dependencies. The live comparison checks full output vectors, all inference, variance components, likelihood and exact group/sample metadata. CSV snapshots, original studies, export versions, checksums and explicit matrix construction are documented in data provenance.
Published near-zero observation-level differences use a documented 1e-6 absolute outcome-unit tolerance plus 1e-6 relative. Other fields use 1e-7 absolute plus 1e-6 relative; likelihood/AIC use 1e-7 absolute plus 1e-10 relative. A separate native-versus-statsmodels check uses the stricter original uniform tolerance. The notebook includes independent profile-score checks and recorded reference optimizer rounding, rather than hiding disagreements or changing model conventions. Run docs/verifications/compare_lmm.py --public in the pinned Python environment.

title: Verification
text:
Expanded R compatibility
The executed audit verifies 12 weighted/offset fixed-estimator cases and 15 general Gaussian mixed cases. Both native BOBYQA and Nelder–Mead are compared against actual lme4 bobyqa, Nelder_Mead, nlminbwrap and nloptwrap reference fits, with saved controls, convergence codes and warnings. The published sleepstudy random-slope model has ML/REML statsmodels checks too. The coverage ledger documents quantity-specific tolerances, backend differences and unsupported features. New fixture tests need no R; compare_r_compatibility.py adds actual PHP and live statsmodels verification.

title: Verification
section: Binomial logit with one random intercept
text:
Binomial logit with one random intercept
tests/fixtures/logistic-mixed-r.json stores seven datasets at four integration settings (Laplace, 9, 25, 61 nodes), including published cbpp data and difficult rare-event/large-variation cases. Rust checks full output against lme4 and tests normal quadrature moments/tiny tail weights, the ordinary-GLM zero-variance reduction, predictor units, count canonicalization/limits and failure controls. PHP integration checks the actual binding, typed labels, complete row alignment, original-input validation, warnings and strict missingness.
The executed verification notebook adds independent SciPy root finding, matched-approximation likelihood evaluation and QUADPACK integration. It distinguishes R agreement from approximation accuracy and retains lme4’s raw likelihood convention plus the disclosed grouped-binomial normalization correction. The full Python mixed-model reference is SciPy; statsmodels’ Bayesian binomial mixed estimator has a different objective.
See the v0.1 stabilization assessment for the offline scripts/check gate, IDE stubs, structured diagnostics, stress fixtures, provenance manifest, performance preservation and remaining release/deployment gates.

title: Gaussian random-intercept ML verification record
text:
The executed comparison fits identical observations in R lme4 ML, Python statsmodels MixedLM ML and PHP fit_mixed_intercept. The saved report records versions, full outputs, Python warnings/backend, covariance convention and differences from R.
Six saved R fixtures cover simulated schools with correlated predictors, a single predictor, no fixed intercept, intercept only, a singleton group and an exact zero-group-variance boundary. Three-way verification adds missingness in predictors, outcomes and group IDs. Independent Rust tests also check a balanced intercept-only sample with analytically known variances and shrinkage. The deterministic tests run without R/Python installed.
Four additional published datasets—sleepstudy, Orthodont, Machines and Hsb82— are checked against both lme4 and nlme saved ML outputs in Rust and PHP. The published-data notebook executes fresh fits in both R packages, statsmodels and PHP and checks every row. See source provenance, tests/fixtures/lmm-public-r.json and the live report. Published-data tolerances retain 1e-7 absolute + 1e-6 relative for ordinary quantities, use 1e-6 absolute + 1e-6 relative for observation-length outputs, and 1e-7 absolute + 1e-10 relative for likelihood/AIC. The notebook documents the measured R optimizer precision limit for near-zero Hsb82 residuals. A separate native-versus-statsmodels check keeps the strict original uniform tolerance.
All fixed-effect inference, covariance, population/conditional fitted values, both residual definitions, group effects, variances, ICC, marginal likelihood and AIC are compared at 1e-7 + 1e-6 × abs(reference). Labels/order and missing positions are exact. Python uses statsmodels estimates with plug-in GLS covariance to match lme4; its native joint-Hessian covariance is a different convention. The boundary fixture’s Python reference is explicitly the NumPy OLS ML limit, not a statsmodels mixed optimizer result.
PHP tests check integer/string group identity, null group deletion, invalid float/boolean labels before deletion, missing warnings and strict rejection. Rust tests check units, row/group order, invalid shapes, unidentified grouping, rank deficiency, perfect fits and unsupported zero-residual-variance limits. An independent observation-level GLS test checks the cached QR reduction at several variance ratios, with correlated predictors and large outcome offsets; it verifies both optimized and arbitrary-coefficient residual norms. The profile search has a finite log-ratio range/grid and is not an exhaustive global optimization proof. The first model has no REML, random slopes, multiple grouping factors, finite-sample df adjustments or variance-component tests. Normal inference with few groups can be unreliable.

export PHP_CONFIG=/opt/homebrew/bin/php-config

title: OLS verification in R, statsmodels and PHP
text: The executable verification notebook shows the same observations, equivalent calls, coefficients, inference and model statistics across all three implementations. ols-results.json contains the saved complete numerical results, inputs, versions, sample metadata, PHP warnings and differences from R. These are generated results, not hand-entered examples. The math notebook derives the calculations.

title: OLS verification in R, statsmodels and PHP
text:
Reproduction
Follow notebook setup to install development tools and build the PHP extension, then run:
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_ols.py
The script fits every case afresh using Rscript, statsmodels and PHP, checks all statistical fields against R with absolute tolerance 1e-9 and relative tolerance 1e-7, and writes ols-results.json. It consumes the ordinary deterministic cases from tests/fixtures/ols-r.json plus an explicit missing-data case. R and Python are optional development tools; cargo test and tests/ols.php still run without them. See verification policy for the tolerance’s limits.

title: OLS verification in R, statsmodels and PHP
text:
Equivalent specifications
For the shared simulated housing dataset in examples/ols.php, run from the repository root:
observations <- read.csv("docs/data/housing.csv")
fit <- lm(monthly_rent ~ area_m2, data = observations, na.action = na.omit)
summary(fit)
confint(fit, level = 0.95)
logLik(fit)
# A second model uses correlated predictors:
summary(lm(monthly_rent ~ area_m2 + bedrooms, data = observations))
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
observations = pd.read_csv("docs/data/housing.csv")
X = sm.add_constant(observations[["area_m2"]])
y = observations["monthly_rent"]
fit = sm.OLS(y, X, missing='drop', hasconst=True).fit(use_t=True)
print(fit.params, fit.bse, fit.tvalues, fit.pvalues, fit.conf_int(), fit.llf)
// The verification runner prepares a complete design from the shared housing CSV.
// Each row of $x is [1.0, area_m2]; $y contains monthly_rent.
$result = Phit\fit_ols(x: $x, y: $y, intercept: false);
These are synthetic apartments, not empirical housing records. The math notebook explains the generating process and reports sample correlations. The fixtures retain small hand-checkable numerical cases alongside these teaching examples.
These use an intercept, conventional homoskedastic covariance, residual variance RSS/(n-p), Student t tests, and 95% intervals. Likelihood uses ML variance RSS/n. The general R runner receives the explicit design columns with formula y ~ . - 1, then calculates R-squared using the same ones-column convention as the extension; this avoids a duplicate intercept. R’s coefficients, covariance, standard errors, tests, intervals, residuals and log-likelihood come from lm(). The notebook displays both the user-facing calls and this runner convention.
Sources: R lm, statsmodels OLS and statsmodels missing data.

All fields pass the stated tolerance for all seven cases. The executable notebook displays the housing coefficients and inference from all three implementations. The saved report records the actual environment: R 4.6.1, statsmodels 0.15.0, NumPy 2.5.4, Python 3.14, and PHP 8.5.10 on the development Mac. This is not evidence of testing Linux or other PHP builds.
For the missing-data case, original positions 1 and 3 are omitted; positions 0, 2, 4 and 5 are retained. PHP emits one E_WARNING with the dropped/original counts and returns sample metadata. The runner checks those positions and counts, and exposes the captured warning in both the saved report and notebook.
Perfect/zero fits and invalid/singular inputs are covered by the Rust/PHP tests, not finite three-way comparisons. Decomposition-dependent tiny residuals make perfect-fit t/p and likelihood comparisons unstable. References may also accept singular designs by aliasing coefficients while our implementation rejects them.

title: Probit regression verification record
text: The executed comparison fits identical observations in base R glm(), statsmodels GLM, and PHP fit_probit(). The saved report records versions, complete outputs, maximum differences from R, warnings and retained-row metadata.

title: Probit regression verification record
text:
Reference cases and conventions
Six saved R fixtures cover the simulated learning sample, a single predictor, multiple predictors, no intercept, intercept only, correlated full-rank columns and imbalanced outcomes (the main sample is the multiple-predictor case). The three-way comparison adds listwise deletion of two rows. All coefficients, covariance entries, standard errors, normal z tests and p-values, Wald confidence limits, full fitted probabilities and response residuals, likelihood, deviance, null deviance, AIC and residual df are checked. Numerical tolerance is 1e-9 + 1e-7 × abs(reference); sample accounting is exact.
R uses confint.default(fit), not profile-likelihood confint(fit). Its fitting tolerance is 1e-16 to make covariance evaluated at the preceding IRLS iterate negligible. Iteration counts can differ across implementations; they are not a reference equality requirement. Without a ones column the null baseline is probability 0.5; the Python runner computes this convention explicitly.

title: Probit regression verification record
text:
Failure and integration checks
Rust/PHP tests reject insufficient observations, invalid shapes, nonfinite or nonbinary outcomes, one-class samples, dependent columns, and selected complete and quasi-separated designs. They check scaled predictor units, stable arithmetic at extreme logits, iteration exhaustion, missing-row warnings and alignment. OLS integration tests also run after changes to the shared PHP conversion code. No penalties or Firth correction are supplied. The separation check is not an exhaustive LP detector, and Wald inference can be poor with sparse or near-separated samples. Linux and PHP-FPM deployment have not been exercised by these reports.

title: Probit regression verification record
text:
Reproduce
From the repository root with matching PHP development tools:
export PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php
export PHP_CONFIG=/opt/homebrew/bin/php-config

cargo build -p phit --locked
